literal: Even if the measure of the incoming path is small, there is no ruin, if the outgoing path does not widen.
translation: Even if the source of income is small in measure, there is no ruin as long as the path of expenditure does not exceed it.
modern: வருமானம் வரும் வழி சிறியதாக இருந்தாலும், செலவு செய்யும் வழி விரிவடையாமல் இருந்தால் அழிவு இல்லை.
explanation: This couplet highlights the fundamental principle of financial management. The poet uses the terms 'āgāṟu' (the incoming path or income) and 'pōgāṟu' (the outgoing path or expenditure) to describe a person's budget. Even if one's income is very small ('iṭṭitu'), there will be no ruin ('kēṭu illai') as long as the expenses do not expand ('agalā') beyond that limit. The conditional word 'kaṭai' (if) emphasizes that financial survival depends entirely on keeping expenditure within the bounds of income.
